prompt: A chain of fitness studios has seen profits fall for two years. The candidate's framework: (1) Membership revenue: members × average fee; (2) Other revenue: retail and personal training; (3) Fixed costs: rent and equipment. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Buckets 1 and 2 overlap: personal training is part of membership
options.feedback: Here personal training is sold on top of the membership fee, so it is separate revenue.

options.text: Bucket 3 doesn't belong: rent and equipment don't change year to year
options.feedback: Even fixed costs can rise, for example at a lease renewal, and they are part of profit. Bucket 3 belongs.

options.text: It's a generic profit tree: a studio decline starts with member churn
options.feedback: A profit tree fits a profit decline, and churn sits inside bucket 1 (members × fee). The flaw is the missing cost line.

options.text: Missing: instructor pay and other costs that grow with classes
options.feedback: Right. Instructor pay is one of the biggest studio costs, and it grows with the number of classes. A cost bucket with only rent and equipment misses it.

explanation: Profit = revenue − all costs. Instructor pay and other variable costs are missing, and they are a large share of studio costs.

extras.corrected_framework: Revenue (members × fee, other income); fixed costs (rent, equipment); variable costs (instructors, utilities, marketing)
